newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: World's poorest to gain from free trade-report.
newsitem.headline: World's poorest to gain from free trade-report.

text.p: The world's poorest countries stand to gain the least from the liberalisation of trade, the U.K.-based Christian Aid said in a report, released as the World Trade Organisation (WTO) began to meet in Singapore on Monday.
The 48 Least Developed Countries (LLDCs) had 12 percent of the world's population but only 0.4 percent of global trade.
These countries with a combined population of 570 million had exports worth less than half of Ireland's.
"There is no level playing field in international trade," said Peter Madden, head of policy and co-author of the report "The Lands that Trade Forgot".
"The WTO should show commitment by at least adopting the proposal for duty free access to rich country markets for the least developed countries," Madden said.
The report called for a set of development objectives to be pursued in trade agreements recognising the needs of the poor, including poverty reduction and food security.
It recommended better access to markets for poor countries, increased technology transfer, aid and debt relief.
The report also noted poorest countries should be protected from negative consequences of the Uruguay round of free trade measures.

"(The WTO) carries sufficient weight to press member countries to spread the benefits of globalisation and liberalisation," the report said, adding that while opportunities did exist, competition was more intense and standards were higher.
